Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações shows no avatar/name/email (still the Story 2.4 toggle-only stub) and has no way to edit the display name (epic-8-context.md's Story 8.3 scope).

**Approach:** Add a profile header (52dp avatar + name/email) above the biometric toggle. A pencil icon switches the name to an inline `AppTextField`; it becomes a check that saves via the existing `account-settings-update` PATCH and reverts to display mode. Tapping away unconfirmed reverts without saving.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `AccountSettingsDto` decodes `displayName`/`email` too (required strings), full-contract-decode precedent as `DashboardNarrativeDto`.
- No new network call: `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s success branch also sets new `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` (default `''`) from that response.
- New `setDisplayName(String)`: own `_nameGeneration` guard (shape of `setBiometricEnabled`'s `_generation`, kept separate), **not optimistic** — await `AccountRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName` (`{'displayName': name}`), set `_currentDisplayName` only on success.
- Cubit reads `displayName`/`email` from the repository at construction. New state: `isEditingName`, `nameDraft`, `isSavingName`, `nameErrorMessage`. New methods: `startEditingName()` (draft = current name), `updateNameDraft()`, `cancelEditingName()` (no-op while saving), `confirmEditingName()` — trims draft; empty/unchanged reverts with no PATCH; otherwise saves, staying in edit mode with the error on failure (draft kept) or reverting with the new name on success.
- Screen: header is the first scroll-`Column` child, above the toggle. `Avatar(size: AvatarSize.large)`, caller derives initials (first letter of first + last word). Name: `textTitleSm`+`colorTextPrimary`. Email: `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle`+`colorTextSecondary`. Icon: `Icons.edit`/`Icons.check`, `dialogIconSize`, `colorPrimary`, in `InkWell`+`ConstrainedBox(minHeight/minWidth: insertionModalTapTargetMin)` (tap-target fix, same as spec-8-2's retry link). Field + check icon in one `TapRegion(onTapOutside: cancelEditingName)`. Field: `AppTextField(controller, errorText: nameErrorMessage)`, no label/hint.
- `_announce` fires on a save failure, same `BlocListener` convention as the toggle's error.
- Keep `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s name even though it now also sets `displayName`/`email` — renaming ripples into `main.dart`/`vault_lock_screen.dart` for no functional gain.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** a second fetch for displayName/email; an optimistic flip for the name; persona/logout/delete UI (Stories 8.4/8.5); merging name-edit into the toggle's own state.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap pencil | `isEditingName: false` | Field replaces name, draft = current, icon -> check | N/A |
| Confirm, changed non-empty name | tap check | PATCH, saving indicator, success -> display mode, new name | Failure -> stays editing, inline error, draft kept |
| Confirm, empty/unchanged draft | tap check | Reverts immediately, no PATCH | N/A |

 - **Finding (blind-hunter + verification-gap review, confirmed):** the original frozen Boundaries line ("announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement") was unconditional — `narrativeCubit.load()` fires on every screen open regardless of count, so a `0`/`1`/mid-range-count user (for whom `DashboardChartSection` never renders the narrative section at all) could still hear a spoken "narrative failed" announcement for a UI element never shown to them. +## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Configurações shows no avatar/name/email (still the Story 2.4 toggle-only stub) and has no way to edit the display name (epic-8-context.md's Story 8.3 scope).
+
+**Approach:** Add a profile header (52dp avatar + name/email) above the biometric toggle. A pencil icon switches the name to an inline `AppTextField`; it becomes a check that saves via the existing `account-settings-update` PATCH and reverts to display mode. Tapping away unconfirmed reverts without saving.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- `AccountSettingsDto` decodes `displayName`/`email` too (required strings), full-contract-decode precedent as `DashboardNarrativeDto`.
+- No new network call: `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s success branch also sets new `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` (default `''`) from that response.
+- New `setDisplayName(String)`: own `_nameGeneration` guard (shape of `setBiometricEnabled`'s `_generation`, kept separate), **not optimistic** — await `AccountRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName` (`{'displayName': name}`), set `_currentDisplayName` only on success.
+- Cubit reads `displayName`/`email` from the repository at construction. New state: `isEditingName`, `nameDraft`, `isSavingName`, `nameErrorMessage`. New methods: `startEditingName()` (draft = current name), `updateNameDraft()`, `cancelEditingName()` (no-op while saving), `confirmEditingName()` — trims draft; empty/unchanged reverts with no PATCH; otherwise saves, staying in edit mode with the error on failure (draft kept) or reverting with the new name on success.
+- Screen: header is the first scroll-`Column` child, above the toggle. `Avatar(size: AvatarSize.large)`, caller derives initials (first letter of first + last word). Name: `textTitleSm`+`colorTextPrimary`. Email: `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle`+`colorTextSecondary`. Icon: `Icons.edit`/`Icons.check`, `dialogIconSize`, `colorPrimary`, in `InkWell`+`ConstrainedBox(minHeight/minWidth: insertionModalTapTargetMin)` (tap-target fix, same as spec-8-2's retry link). Field + check icon in one `TapRegion(onTapOutside: cancelEditingName)`. Field: `AppTextField(controller, errorText: nameErrorMessage)`, no label/hint.
+- `_announce` fires on a save failure, same `BlocListener` convention as the toggle's error.
+- Keep `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s name even though it now also sets `displayName`/`email` — renaming ripples into `main.dart`/`vault_lock_screen.dart` for no functional gain.
+
+**Ask First:** None.
+
+**Never:** a second fetch for displayName/email; an optimistic flip for the name; persona/logout/delete UI (Stories 8.4/8.5); merging name-edit into the toggle's own state.
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Tap pencil | `isEditingName: false` | Field replaces name, draft = current, icon -> check | N/A |
+| Confirm, changed non-empty name | tap check | PATCH, saving indicator, success -> display mode, new name | Failure -> stays editing, inline error, draft kept |
+| Confirm, empty/unchanged draft | tap check | Reverts immediately, no PATCH | N/A |
+| Tap away, not saving | outside tap | Reverts, draft discarded, no PATCH | N/A |
+| Tap away, saving | outside tap | No-op, save completes | N/A |

+
+## Tasks & Acceptance
+
+**Execution:**
+- [x] `account_settings_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- decode `displayName`/`email`

  ### Server-echoed `displayName` from `setDisplayName` never reaches the UI
  
  - **Changed surface:** `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl.setDisplayName`'s success branch sets `_currentDisplayName` from the response's own echoed `dto.displayName`, not the locally-sent name (`lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:168-175`). `AccountSettingsCubit.confirmEditingName`'s success branch, however, emits `displayName: trimmed` — the locally-typed string — rather than re-reading the repository's corrected value (`lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:286-296`, specifically line 291).
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `AccountSettingsScreen._buildNameRow`/`_buildProfileHeader`, which render `state.displayName` straight from the cubit (`lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:117`, `:210`, `:218`, `:325`) — the cubit's `displayName` is what the user actually sees, and the domain `setDisplayName` signature (`Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>`) gives the cubit no way to observe the echoed value at all.
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** `test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart:512-521` ("on success, currentDisplayName is set from the response's own echoed displayName, not the locally-sent name") only asserts the repository's internal field in isolation. `test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart:308` and `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart:783-801` ("confirming a changed, non-empty name...") both stub `setDisplayNameResult = right(unit)` with no distinct echoed value, so neither test can distinguish the locally-sent name from a server-normalized one.
  - **Missing verification:** no test configures a fake repository (or the real one) to echo back a `displayName` that differs from what was sent, then asserts the cubit's/screen's displayed name reflects that server-corrected value rather than the user's raw input.
  - **Demonstration:** if the backend normalizes the name on write (trims extra internal whitespace, re-cases it, etc.), `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl.currentDisplayName` correctly holds the normalized value, but the cubit's `confirmEditingName` still emits the locally-computed `trimmed` string, so the screen keeps showing the user's raw, un-normalized input for the rest of that singleton cubit's lifetime. None of the tests above would fail, because their fakes never model a differing echo.
  - **Consequence:** after a successful edit where the server's stored name differs from what was typed, the UI silently diverges from the account's actual name, and the "echo wins" correctness fix added at the repository layer never actually reaches anything a user sees within the same session.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a cubit-level test (using a fake whose `currentDisplayName` getter returns a different value than the argument passed to `setDisplayName`) asserting `cubit.state.displayName` equals the repository's post-success value, not the locally-sent one.
  
  ### Name-save failure's VoiceOver announcement is unverified
  
  - **Changed surface:** the new `BlocListener<AccountSettingsCubit, AccountSettingsState>` that calls `_announce(state.nameErrorMessage!)` whenever `nameErrorMessage` transitions to a new non-null value (`lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:306-317`), per Boundaries: "`_announce` fires on a save failure, same `BlocListener` convention as the toggle's error".

  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** that test asserts only `find.byType(TextField)`, the controller's text, and `find.text('Sem conexão')` — it never calls `interceptAnnouncements` (`test/support/intercept_announcements.dart`), whose own doc comment states plain-widget assertions "would still pass even if a `_announce()` call were deleted or its guard inverted."
  - **Missing verification:** no assertion that the accessibility channel actually receives the failure message (e.g. via `interceptAnnouncements(tester)` and checking the captured list) when a name save fails.
  - **Demonstration:** deleting the new `BlocListener`, inverting its `listenWhen`, or passing the wrong message would still pass the existing failed-save test, since it only reads `Text`/`TextField` widgets and never intercepts `SystemChannels.accessibility`.
  - **Consequence:** a regression silencing or breaking the save-failure VoiceOver announcement — the one path the Boundaries explicitly call for — ships with the full suite green.
  - **Suggested test shape:** reuse `interceptAnnouncements(tester)` (as the sibling toggle-failure and narrative-failure tests already do in this same file) in a widget test that fails a name save and asserts the captured announcements contain the failure message.

  - **Changed surface:** `if (isClosed) { return; }` immediately after `await _repository.setDisplayName(trimmed)` in `AccountSettingsCubit.confirmEditingName` (`lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:265-269`), guarding against emitting on a closed `Cubit` — the same race `toggleBiometric`'s own identical guard defends against, per its comment "Same close()-race guard as toggleBiometric's own."
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `AccountSettingsCubit` itself, a DI lazy singleton whose `dispose:` hook calls `close()` (per the cubit's own class doc, anticipating a future logout).
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** `grep -rn "confirmEditingName" test/` shows it is referenced only in `test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart` and `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart`. Neither file has a test that calls `cubit.close()` (or disposes the screen) while a `confirmEditingName()` call's `setDisplayName` await is still pending — confirmed by reading every `group`/`test` block in the cubit test file (lines 122-399 range) and the profile-header group in the screen test file.
  - **Missing verification:** no test holds `setDisplayName` unresolved (the fakes in both files already support this via `setDisplayNameGate`, used elsewhere in the same diff for the "no-op while saving" cases), calls `close()` mid-flight, then resolves the gate and asserts no `StateError` is thrown.
  - **Demonstration:** removing `if (isClosed) { return; }` would only throw `StateError('Cannot emit new states after calling close')` once `setDisplayName` resolves after `close()` — a sequence no existing test constructs, so it would pass the whole suite undetected.
  - **Consequence:** a future refactor that drops this guard ships an uncaught `StateError` whenever the cubit is disposed while a name save is in flight, with the full suite green.
  - **Suggested test shape:** same shape as this very diff's own new `dashboard_narrative_cubit_test.dart` test "close() while a load() is in flight never throws" (`test/features/dashboard/presentation/cubit/dashboard_narrative_cubit_test.dart:237-248`) — hold `setDisplayNameGate`, call `cubit.close()` mid-flight, complete the gate, assert no exception.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

16	/// Tela 6 — Configurações, Story 2.4's real build (Acceptance Criteria:
17	/// "shows only the biometric toggle — minimal, Epic 8 extends it, never
18	/// rebuilds it") extended by spec-8-1 with the "Sua evolução" chart
19	/// section below the toggle, and by spec-8-2 with its independent AI
20	/// narrative fetch. Replaces the former `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
21	class AccountSettingsScreen extends StatefulWidget {
22	  const AccountSettingsScreen({
23	    required this.cubit,
24	    required this.dashboardCubit,
25	    required this.narrativeCubit,
26	    super.key,
27	  });
28	
29	  final AccountSettingsCubit cubit;
30	
31	  /// spec-8-1 — the "Sua evolução" chart section's own cubit, a DI
32	  /// `lazySingleton` like [cubit] (Code Map); this `StatefulWidget` never
33	  /// closes it either, same rationale [cubit]'s own doc already gives.
34	  final DashboardCubit dashboardCubit;
35	
36	  /// spec-8-2 — the chart section's own independent AI narrative fetch, a
37	  /// second DI `lazySingleton` like [dashboardCubit] above (Boundaries:
38	  /// "two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the
39	  /// other").
40	  final DashboardNarrativeCubit narrativeCubit;
41	
42	  @override
43	  State<AccountSettingsScreen> createState() => _AccountSettingsScreenState();
44	}
45	
46	class _AccountSettingsScreenState extends State<AccountSettingsScreen> {
47	  /// spec-8-3 — the inline name field's own controller. Its text is kept
48	  /// in sync with `AccountSettingsState.nameDraft` only when entering edit
49	  /// mode (the `BlocListener` below); while editing, the field's own
50	  /// `onChanged` is this screen's single source for both the controller's
51	  /// displayed text and the cubit's `nameDraft`.
52	  late final TextEditingController _nameController;
53	
54	  @override
55	  void initState() {
56	    super.initState();
57	    _nameController = TextEditingController();
58	    // Review finding: clears a leftover error from a previous visit's
59	    // failed toggle — this cubit is a DI singleton, so without this a
60	    // stale message would still be showing on an unrelated later visit.
61	    widget.cubit.clearStaleError();
62	    // Boundaries: "`AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls
63	    // `dashboardCubit.load()` unconditionally... so every open is a live
64	    // fetch, never the singleton's stale state" (FR-09: "computed on
65	    // demand, never stale").
66	    widget.dashboardCubit.load();
67	    // spec-8-2 — fired alongside the call above, neither awaiting the
68	    // other (Boundaries: "two independent fetches fired in parallel").
69	    widget.narrativeCubit.load();
70	  }
71	
72	  @override
73	  void dispose() {
74	    _nameController.dispose();
75	    super.dispose();
76	  }
77	
78	  /// spec-8-3 — caller derives initials from the display name (Boundaries):
79	  /// first letter of the first word plus first letter of the last word (a
80	  /// single-word name yields one letter) — `Avatar` itself only renders
81	  /// whatever it's given, uppercased.
82	  ///
83	  /// Code-review patch: extracts each initial via `Characters.first`
84	  /// (Unicode grapheme-cluster aware), not `String.substring(0, 1)` —
85	  /// `substring` slices by UTF-16 code unit, which would split an astral-
86	  /// plane character (e.g. an emoji) that starts a word into an unpaired
87	  /// surrogate half.
88	  String _initialsFor(String name) {
89	    final words = name
90	        .trim()
91	        .split(RegExp(r'\s+'))
92	        .where((w) => w.isNotEmpty)
93	        .toList();
94	    if (words.isEmpty) {
95	      return '';
96	    }
97	    final first = words.first.characters.first;
98	    if (words.length == 1) {
99	      return first;
100	    }
101	    final last = words.last.characters.first;
102	    return '$first$last';
103	  }
104	
105	  /// spec-8-3 — the profile header: 52dp avatar + name/email, the pencil-
106	  /// becomes-check inline name edit (Intent/Boundaries). Built from
107	  /// `AccountSettingsState` directly, same "cubit is the single source"
108	  /// convention the rest of this screen already follows.
109	  Widget _buildNameRow(BuildContext context, AccountSettingsState state) {
110	    final cubit = context.read<AccountSettingsCubit>();
111	    if (!state.isEditingName) {
112	      return Row(
113	        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
114	        children: [
115	          Flexible(
116	            child: Text(
117	              state.displayName,
118	              style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(
119	                color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
120	              ),
121	              // Code-review patch: the backend allows a displayName up to
122	              // 80 characters — without this, a long name wraps to
123	              // multiple lines inside this `Flexible`, misaligning against
124	              // the fixed-size pencil icon beside it.
125	              maxLines: 1,
126	              overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
127	            ),
128	          ),
129	          const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
130	          Semantics(
131	            button: true,
132	            label: 'Editar nome',
133	            excludeSemantics: true,
134	            child: InkWell(
135	              onTap: cubit.startEditingName,
136	              child: ConstrainedBox(
137	                constraints: const BoxConstraints(
138	                  minWidth: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
139	                  minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
140	                ),
141	                child: const Icon(
142	                  Icons.edit,
143	                  size: DesignTokens.dialogIconSize,
144	                  color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
145	                ),
146	              ),
147	            ),
148	          ),
149	        ],
150	      );
151	    }
152	
153	    // Boundaries: "Field + check icon in one TapRegion(onTapOutside:
154	    // cancelEditingName)" — a tap anywhere outside this field+icon pair
155	    // reverts the unconfirmed edit, no PATCH sent.
156	    return TapRegion(
157	      onTapOutside: (_) => cubit.cancelEditingName(),
158	      child: Row(
159	        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
160	        children: [
161	          Expanded(
162	            child: AppTextField(
163	              controller: _nameController,
164	              errorText: state.nameErrorMessage,
165	              onChanged: cubit.updateNameDraft,
166	            ),
167	          ),
168	          const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
169	          if (state.isSavingName)
170	            const SizedBox(
171	              width: DesignTokens.accountSettingsSavingIndicatorSize,
172	              height: DesignTokens.accountSettingsSavingIndicatorSize,
173	              child: CircularProgressIndicator(
174	                strokeWidth:
175	                    DesignTokens.accountSettingsSavingIndicatorStrokeWidth,
176	                color: DesignTokens.colorAccent,
177	              ),
178	            )
179	          else
180	            Semantics(
181	              button: true,
182	              label: 'Salvar nome',
183	              excludeSemantics: true,
184	              child: InkWell(
185	                onTap: cubit.confirmEditingName,
186	                child: ConstrainedBox(
187	                  constraints: const BoxConstraints(
188	                    minWidth: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
189	                    minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
190	                  ),
191	                  child: const Icon(
192	                    Icons.check,
193	                    size: DesignTokens.dialogIconSize,
194	                    color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
195	                  ),
196	                ),
197	              ),
198	            ),
199	        ],
200	      ),
201	    );
202	  }

204	  Widget _buildProfileHeader(BuildContext context, AccountSettingsState state) {
205	    return Row(
206	      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
207	      children: [
208	        Avatar(
209	          size: AvatarSize.large,
210	          initials: _initialsFor(state.displayName),
211	        ),
212	        const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingMd),
213	        Expanded(
214	          child: Column(
215	            crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
216	            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
217	            children: [
218	              _buildNameRow(context, state),
219	              const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
220	              Text(
221	                state.email,
222	                style: DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle.copyWith(
223	                  color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
224	                ),
225	              ),
226	            ],
227	          ),
228	        ),
229	      ],
230	    );
231	  }
232	
233	  // Review finding: mirrors `vault_lock_screen.dart`'s own `_announce` —
234	  // VoiceOver (this app is iOS-only) doesn't reliably treat a live-region
235	  // subtree update as an announcement on its own, so a failed/reverted
236	  // toggle is spoken explicitly here instead.
237	  Future<void> _announce(String message) async {
238	    if (!mounted) {
239	      return;
240	    }
241	    await SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(
242	      View.of(context),
243	      message,
244	      TextDirection.ltr,
245	    );
246	  }
247	
248	  @override
249	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
250	    return MultiBlocProvider(
251	      providers: [
252	        BlocProvider.value(value: widget.cubit),
253	        // spec-8-1 — makes `DashboardCubit` available to
254	        // `DashboardChartSection` below, same two-cubit convention
255	        // `MeusRegistrosScreen` already uses for its own `cubit`/
256	        // `searchCubit` pair.
257	        BlocProvider.value(value: widget.dashboardCubit),
258	        // spec-8-2 — makes `DashboardNarrativeCubit` available to
259	        // `DashboardChartSection`'s own narrative section, same
260	        // convention as `dashboardCubit` above.
261	        BlocProvider.value(value: widget.narrativeCubit),
262	      ],
263	      child: Scaffold(
264	        backgroundColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceBg,
265	        body: Column(
266	          children: [
267	            const BackArrowHeader(title: 'Configurações'),
268	            // spec-8-1 — now `Expanded` + scrollable: the toggle alone
269	            // always fit unscrolled, but the chart section below it can
270	            // grow past the available height on a shorter device/larger
271	            // text scale (Design Notes: "decide and proceed" — neither
272	            // `prototype-extract.md` nor the frozen spec says whether this
273	            // screen scrolls).
274	            Expanded(
275	              child: SingleChildScrollView(
276	                padding: DesignTokens.screenPadding,
277	                child: Column(
278	                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
279	                  children: [
280	                    // spec-8-3 — Code Map: "header is the first scroll-
281	                    // Column child, above the toggle".
282	                    MultiBlocListener(
283	                      listeners: [
284	                        // Syncs the field's controller only at the moment
285	                        // editing starts — while editing, the field's own
286	                        // `onChanged` (-> `updateNameDraft`) is this
287	                        // screen's single source for both the
288	                        // controller's displayed text and the cubit's own
289	                        // `nameDraft`.
290	                        BlocListener<
291	                          AccountSettingsCubit,
292	                          AccountSettingsState
293	                        >(
294	                          listenWhen: (previous, current) =>
295	                              !previous.isEditingName && current.isEditingName,
296	                          listener: (context, state) {
297	                            _nameController.text = state.nameDraft;
298	                            _nameController.selection = TextSelection.collapsed(
299	                              offset: _nameController.text.length,
300	                            );
301	                          },
302	                        ),
303	                        // Boundaries: "`_announce` fires on a save
304	                        // failure, same `BlocListener` convention as the
305	                        // toggle's error".
306	                        BlocListener<
307	                          AccountSettingsCubit,
308	                          AccountSettingsState
309	                        >(
310	                          listenWhen: (previous, current) =>
311	                              current.nameErrorMessage != null &&
312	                              current.nameErrorMessage !=
313	                                  previous.nameErrorMessage,
314	                          listener: (context, state) {
315	                            _announce(state.nameErrorMessage!);
316	                          },
317	                        ),
318	                      ],
319	                      child:
320	                          BlocBuilder<
321	                            AccountSettingsCubit,
322	                            AccountSettingsState
323	                          >(
324	                            builder: (context, state) =>
325	                                _buildProfileHeader(context, state),
326	                          ),
327	                    ),
328	                    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXl),
329	                    BlocConsumer<AccountSettingsCubit, AccountSettingsState>(
330	                      listener: (context, state) {
331	                        if (state.errorMessage != null) {
332	                          _announce(state.errorMessage!);
333	                        }
334	                      },
335	                      builder: (context, state) {
336	                        return Column(
337	                          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
338	                          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
339	                          children: [
340	                            MergeSemantics(
341	                              child: Semantics(
342	                                label: 'Entrar com biometria',
343	                                child: Row(
344	                                  children: [
345	                                    Expanded(
346	                                      child: ExcludeSemantics(
347	                                        child: Text(
348	                                          'Entrar com biometria',
349	                                          style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg
350	                                              .copyWith(
351	                                                color: DesignTokens
352	                                                    .colorTextPrimary,
353	                                              ),
354	                                        ),
355	                                      ),
356	                                    ),
357	                                    if (state.isSaving) ...[
358	                                      const SizedBox(
359	                                        width: DesignTokens
360	                                            .accountSettingsSavingIndicatorSize,
361	                                        height: DesignTokens
362	                                            .accountSettingsSavingIndicatorSize,
363	                                        child: CircularProgressIndicator(
364	                                          strokeWidth: DesignTokens
365	                                              .accountSettingsSavingIndicatorStrokeWidth,
366	                                          color: DesignTokens.colorAccent,
367	                                        ),
368	                                      ),
369	                                      const SizedBox(
370	                                        width: DesignTokens.spacingSm,
371	                                      ),
372	                                    ],
373	                                    Switch(
374	                                      value: state.biometricEnabled,
375	                                      // Boundaries: "no new tokens" — reuses
376	                                      // `colorAccent` (Design Notes).
377	                                      activeThumbColor:
378	                                          DesignTokens.colorAccent,
379	                                      // Review finding: `null` while a
380	                                      // toggle is already in flight
381	                                      // (`state.isSaving`) — a disabled
382	                                      // `Switch` can't be tapped again, so a
383	                                      // double-tap can never start a
384	                                      // second, overlapping
385	                                      // `toggleBiometric` call.
386	                                      onChanged: state.isSaving
387	                                          ? null
388	                                          : (value) => context
389	                                                .read<AccountSettingsCubit>()
390	                                                .toggleBiometric(value),
391	                                    ),
392	                                  ],
393	                                ),
394	                              ),
395	                            ),
396	                            if (state.errorMessage != null) ...[
397	                              const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
398	                              Text(
399	                                state.errorMessage!,
400	                                style: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(
401	                                  color: DesignTokens.colorError,
402	                                ),
403	                              ),
404	                            ],
405	                          ],
406	                        );
407	                      },
408	                    ),
409	                    // spec-8-1 — "Sua evolução", sibling to the biometric
410	                    // toggle section above (Code Map: "insert chart as
411	                    // sibling Column child").
412	                    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXl),
413	                    // Review finding: unlike the biometric toggle's own
414	                    // `BlocConsumer` above, the chart section previously
415	                    // never announced its own fetch failures to
416	                    // VoiceOver — a `ResourceError` only ever showed as
417	                    // silent inline text. Reuses the same [_announce]
418	                    // this `State` already uses for the toggle's error,
419	                    // same "VoiceOver doesn't reliably treat a live-region
420	                    // update as an announcement on its own" rationale.
421	                    MultiBlocListener(
422	                      listeners: [
423	                        BlocListener<
424	                          DashboardCubit,
425	                          Resource<DashboardAggregate>
426	                        >(
427	                          listener: (context, state) {
428	                            if (state is ResourceError<DashboardAggregate>) {
429	                              _announce(state.failure.message);
430	                            }
431	                          },
432	                        ),
433	                        // Spec Change Log (spec-8-2 amendment) — the
434	                        // original unconditional version of this listener
435	                        // could speak a narrative-failed announcement for
436	                        // a user whose screen never shows the narrative
437	                        // section at all (0/1/mid-range counts), in
438	                        // tension with the adjacent frozen "Never: show
439	                        // narrative text or its error for 0/1-count
440	                        // states" line. Gated on `DashboardCubit`'s own
441	                        // *current* state — read directly via
442	                        // `context.read`, never merged with this
443	                        // `Resource<String>` into one state object (the
444	                        // "Never: couple the two Resources" line is
445	                        // unaffected) — and announces the same fixed copy
446	                        // the narrative section itself renders
447	                        // (`DashboardChartSection.narrativeUnavailableMessage`)
448	                        // rather than the raw, unsanitized `Failure.
449	                        // message`, so VoiceOver and sighted users hear/
450	                        // read the same wording for the same failure.
451	                        BlocListener<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>(
452	                          listener: (context, state) {
453	                            if (state is! ResourceError<String>) {
454	                              return;
455	                            }
456	                            final dashboardState = context
457	                                .read<DashboardCubit>()
458	                                .state;
459	                            if (dashboardState
460	                                    is ResourceData<DashboardAggregate> &&
461	                                dashboardState.data.totalCount > 30) {
462	                              _announce(
463	                                DashboardChartSection
464	                                    .narrativeUnavailableMessage,
465	                              );
466	                            }
467	                          },
468	                        ),
469	                        // Review finding: the listener above only reads
470	                        // `DashboardNarrativeCubit`'s *current* state at
471	                        // the instant `DashboardCubit` itself transitions
472	                        // past 30 — but the two fetches race independently
473	                        // (Boundaries: "neither awaiting the other"), so
474	                        // the narrative can just as easily resolve to
475	                        // `ResourceError` *before* the aggregate ever
476	                        // reaches `totalCount > 30`. Without this sibling
477	                        // listener that ordering silently drops the
478	                        // announcement forever for that screen-open, even
479	                        // though the error text later becomes visible once
480	                        // the aggregate resolves — the exact VoiceOver/
481	                        // on-screen desync the amendment above exists to
482	                        // prevent. Same read-only, ungated-state check as
483	                        // the listener above, just triggered from the
484	                        // other cubit's own transition.
485	                        BlocListener<
486	                          DashboardCubit,
487	                          Resource<DashboardAggregate>
488	                        >(
489	                          listener: (context, state) {
490	                            if (state is! ResourceData<DashboardAggregate> ||
491	                                state.data.totalCount <= 30) {
492	                              return;
493	                            }
494	                            final narrativeState = context
495	                                .read<DashboardNarrativeCubit>()
496	                                .state;
497	                            if (narrativeState is ResourceError<String>) {
498	                              _announce(
499	                                DashboardChartSection
500	                                    .narrativeUnavailableMessage,
501	                              );
502	                            }
503	                          },
504	                        ),
505	                      ],
506	                      child: const DashboardChartSection(),
507	                    ),
508	                  ],
509	                ),
510	              ),
511	            ),
512	          ],
513	        ),
514	      ),
515	    );
516	  }
517	}

1	---
2	title: 'Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-07'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: []
8	baseline_commit: 'dd59fc845883a9e56ace167dadcdb435744ecf50'
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Configurações shows no avatar/name/email (still the Story 2.4 toggle-only stub) and has no way to edit the display name (epic-8-context.md's Story 8.3 scope).
16	
17	**Approach:** Add a profile header (52dp avatar + name/email) above the biometric toggle. A pencil icon switches the name to an inline `AppTextField`; it becomes a check that saves via the existing `account-settings-update` PATCH and reverts to display mode. Tapping away unconfirmed reverts without saving.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- `AccountSettingsDto` decodes `displayName`/`email` too (required strings), full-contract-decode precedent as `DashboardNarrativeDto`.
23	- No new network call: `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s success branch also sets new `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` (default `''`) from that response.
24	- New `setDisplayName(String)`: own `_nameGeneration` guard (shape of `setBiometricEnabled`'s `_generation`, kept separate), **not optimistic** — await `AccountRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName` (`{'displayName': name}`), set `_currentDisplayName` only on success.
25	- Cubit reads `displayName`/`email` from the repository at construction. New state: `isEditingName`, `nameDraft`, `isSavingName`, `nameErrorMessage`. New methods: `startEditingName()` (draft = current name), `updateNameDraft()`, `cancelEditingName()` (no-op while saving), `confirmEditingName()` — trims draft; empty/unchanged reverts with no PATCH; otherwise saves, staying in edit mode with the error on failure (draft kept) or reverting with the new name on success.
26	- Screen: header is the first scroll-`Column` child, above the toggle. `Avatar(size: AvatarSize.large)`, caller derives initials (first letter of first + last word). Name: `textTitleSm`+`colorTextPrimary`. Email: `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle`+`colorTextSecondary`. Icon: `Icons.edit`/`Icons.check`, `dialogIconSize`, `colorPrimary`, in `InkWell`+`ConstrainedBox(minHeight/minWidth: insertionModalTapTargetMin)` (tap-target fix, same as spec-8-2's retry link). Field + check icon in one `TapRegion(onTapOutside: cancelEditingName)`. Field: `AppTextField(controller, errorText: nameErrorMessage)`, no label/hint.
27	- `_announce` fires on a save failure, same `BlocListener` convention as the toggle's error.
28	- Keep `fetchBiometricEnabled()`'s name even though it now also sets `displayName`/`email` — renaming ripples into `main.dart`/`vault_lock_screen.dart` for no functional gain.
29	
30	**Ask First:** None.
31	
32	**Never:** a second fetch for displayName/email; an optimistic flip for the name; persona/logout/delete UI (Stories 8.4/8.5); merging name-edit into the toggle's own state.
33	
34	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
35	
36	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
37	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
38	| Tap pencil | `isEditingName: false` | Field replaces name, draft = current, icon -> check | N/A |
39	| Confirm, changed non-empty name | tap check | PATCH, saving indicator, success -> display mode, new name | Failure -> stays editing, inline error, draft kept |
40	| Confirm, empty/unchanged draft | tap check | Reverts immediately, no PATCH | N/A |
41	| Tap away, not saving | outside tap | Reverts, draft discarded, no PATCH | N/A |
42	| Tap away, saving | outside tap | No-op, save completes | N/A |
43	
44	</frozen-after-approval>
45	
46	## Code Map
47	
48	- `lib/features/account/data/models/account_settings_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- add `displayName`/`email`
49	- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart:11-47` -- add `updateDisplayName`, mirrors `updateBiometricEnabled`
50	- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart:15-58` -- add `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail`/`setDisplayName`
51	- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:20-139` -- fields + boot-fetch piggyback + `setDisplayName`
52	- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart` -- state/methods per Boundaries
53	- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:104-120` -- header, `TapRegion`, initials helper, `_announce`
54	- `lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart` / `app_text_field.dart` -- reused as-is (first real `AvatarSize.large` consumer)
55	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1737-1819` -- `PATCH /account/settings` (frozen), `displayName` optional, `minLength:1`/`maxLength:80`; `README.md:45` maps it to `account-settings-update`
56	- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:116` + raw prototype `toggleEditProfile`/`saveProfile`/`editIcon` -- pencil/check UX source
57	- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-8-context.md` -- authoritative AC source (no FR in `requirements.md` covers this)
58	- `test/features/account/**` -- extend `_FakeAccountSettingsRepository` + new coverage
59	
60	## Tasks & Acceptance
61	
62	**Execution:**
63	- [x] `account_settings_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- decode `displayName`/`email`
64	- [x] `account_remote_data_source.dart` -- `updateDisplayName`
65	- [x] `account_settings_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- getters + `setDisplayName`, boot-fetch piggyback
66	- [x] `account_settings_cubit.dart` -- edit/draft/save/cancel state machine
67	- [x] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- header, inline edit, `TapRegion`, tap-target fix, announcement
68	- [x] Tests: I/O matrix + the 3 RNF09 failure types for `updateDisplayName`; update existing fakes for the widened interface
69	
70	**Acceptance Criteria:**
71	- Given display mode, when the pencil is tapped, then the name becomes editable (pre-filled) and the icon becomes a check.
72	- Given a changed non-empty draft, when the check is tapped and save succeeds, then the screen shows the new name in display mode.
73	- Given a save fails, then the field stays editable with the typed text and an inline error.
74	- Given an unconfirmed edit, when the user taps outside the field/icon, then the screen reverts with no change sent.
75	
76	## Verification
77	
78	**Commands:**
79	- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- expected: DTO regenerated, no conflicts
80	- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
81	- `fvm flutter test test/features/account` -- expected: all pass
82	
83	**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
84	- Open Configurações; edit through success/failure/tap-away/empty-draft paths per the I/O matrix — widget tests stand in for no device/simulator.
85	
86	## Suggested Review Order
87	
88	**Edit/draft/save/cancel state machine**
89	
90	- Entry point — the check-icon tap: trims the draft, skips the PATCH for an empty/unchanged name, otherwise saves and resolves to the new name or an inline error.
91	  [`account_settings_cubit.dart:258`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart#L258)
92	- Pencil-tap: seeds the draft from the current name, clears any leftover error.
93	  [`account_settings_cubit.dart:223`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart#L223)
94	- Tap-away/cancel: reverts with no PATCH, but is a no-op while a save is already in flight.
95	  [`account_settings_cubit.dart:244`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart#L244)
96	
97	**Repository write path & generation guards (code-review patch)**
98	
99	- `setDisplayName`'s own, separate generation counter — not optimistic, and now sets `_currentDisplayName` from the response's own echoed value rather than the locally-sent one.
100	  [`account_settings_repository_impl.dart:152`](../../lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart#L152)
101	- The boot-fetch piggyback — captures `_nameGeneration` at its own start so a concurrent, already-succeeded `setDisplayName` can never be clobbered by a stale fetch resolving afterward.
102	  [`account_settings_repository_impl.dart:102`](../../lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart#L102)
103	
104	**Contract widening**
105	
106	- `AccountSettingsDto` now decodes `displayName`/`email` as required strings, same full-contract-decode precedent as `DashboardNarrativeDto`.
107	  [`account_settings_dto.dart:16`](../../lib/features/account/data/models/account_settings_dto.dart#L16)
108	- The new write call, mirroring `updateBiometricEnabled`'s own shape.
109	  [`account_remote_data_source.dart:31`](../../lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart#L31)
110	
111	**Inline-edit UI**
112	
113	- The profile header: avatar + name/email, inserted as the scroll column's first child above the toggle.
114	  [`account_settings_screen.dart:204`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart#L204)
115	- The pencil/field-and-check row, including the `TapRegion` that scopes tap-away-to-revert to exactly the field+icon pair.
116	  [`account_settings_screen.dart:109`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart#L109)
117	- Initials extraction — grapheme-cluster aware (`.characters.first`), a code-review patch over the original surrogate-pair-unsafe `substring(0,1)`.
118	  [`account_settings_screen.dart:88`](../../lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart#L88)
119	
120	**Tests**
121	
122	- The full inline-edit I/O & Edge-Case Matrix against the real cubit.
123	  [`account_settings_cubit_test.dart`](../../test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart)
124	- The four Acceptance Criteria proved against the real screen widget, via a profile-aware pump helper.
125	  [`account_settings_screen_test.dart`](../../test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart)
126	- The stale-fetch-vs-saved-name race and response-echo-wins regressions added during code review.
127	  [`account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`](../../test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart)

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap pencil | `isEditingName: false` | Field replaces name, draft = current, icon -> check | N/A |
| Confirm, changed non-empty name | tap check | PATCH, saving indicator, success -> display mode, new name | Failure -> stays editing, inline error, draft kept |
| Confirm, empty/unchanged draft | tap check | Reverts immediately, no PATCH | N/A |
| Tap away, not saving | outside tap | Reverts, draft discarded, no PATCH | N/A |
| Tap away, saving | outside tap | No-op, save completes | N/A |

The cubit never re-reads the repository after construction, so a divergence persists for the rest of the singleton's session. [account_settings_cubit.dart:291]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] The new sibling `BlocListener<DashboardCubit, Resource<DashboardAggregate>>` added to catch the narrative-errors-before-aggregate-resolves race has no `listenWhen` — it re-announces "narrativa indisponível" on every subsequent `DashboardCubit` emission with `totalCount > 30` (e.g. each further entry save via `confirmedWrites`) for as long as the narrative stays in `ResourceError`, not just once for the missed transition the fix was written for. [account_settings_screen.dart:485-504]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_nameController` is created empty in `initState()` on every mount; the only sync (`BlocListener` on the `!previous.isEditingName && current.isEditingName` transition) fires on state *transitions*, not on initial build. Leaving Configurações mid-edit (e.g. via the back arrow, which never calls `cancelEditingName`) and reopening it shows a blank field while the cubit's singleton state still holds `isEditingName: true` with the old `nameDraft` — tapping the check icon in that state silently saves the stale, invisible draft rather than the (empty) field the user sees. [account_settings_screen.dart:52-57]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `fetchBiometricEnabled()` checks `generation != _generation` and returns early *before* ever checking `nameGeneration == _nameGeneration` — a fetch superseded only on its biometric-toggle generation (e.g. the double boot-time call in `main.dart`/`CerneApp.initState()` racing past the 2s `main()` timeout) discards its own still-valid `displayName`/`email` piggyback too, even though no `setDisplayName` call happened in between. [account_settings_repository_impl.dart:111-144]

[test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart:68-80]

- [x] [Review][Defer] `confirmEditingName()`'s `if (isClosed) return;` guard (same close()-race shape as `toggleBiometric`'s own) has no dedicated test — mirrors `toggleBiometric`'s own identical, also-untested guard, not a gap newly introduced for this feature. [account_settings_cubit.dart:267]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_nameGeneration` only orders this client's own local state; it can't prevent the backend itself from processing two overlapping `setDisplayName` PATCH requests out of order, so a locally-"superseded" call's name could still be the one actually persisted server-side. Same residual risk class the existing `_generation` guard already carries for the biometric toggle, not fixable from the client given the frozen contract. [account_settings_repository_impl.dart:152-176]
- [x] [Review][Defer] The `DashboardNarrativeCubit.confirmedWrites` "no `onError` handler" observation is recorded nearly verbatim in both `deferred-work.md` and spec-8-2's own Review Findings, with no cross-reference between the two — a future fix to one is likely to leave the other stale.
